messages:
ishaan: Heads up — installed the Windows MSI on a shared dev VM (Server 2019) and redwoodctl auth login completed in the browser but the regular user account can't run commands afterwards. Error: `failed to read token: access denied`. Token file appears under `C:\Users\Administrator\AppData\Roaming\Redwood	oken.json`. Installer ran as Admin and wrote to admin profile. Anyone seen the MSI write-permissions issue for multi-user machines?

marie: Yikes. We should never drop tokens into a single user's AppData when installer runs elevated. The CLI expects `%APPDATA%\Redwood` but the installer path depended on the user who executed MSI.

priya: Short term: stop the service and copy token to the user's profile, then `icacls` to set proper ACLs. Long term: installer needs to either: (A) offer a per-machine install location and a `redwoodctl service install --system` mode, or (B) set a per-user default and refuse to write tokens to Admin when run elevated. Also we could support a system-wide token store at `C:\ProgramData\Redwood	okens` with ACLs.

ishaan: For me the workaround was:
```
# admin powershell
Copy-Item "C:\Users\Administrator\AppData\Roaming\Redwood\token.json" "C:\Users\ishaan\AppData\Roaming\Redwood\token.json" -Force
icacls "C:\Users\ishaan\AppData\Roaming\Redwood\token.json" /grant ishaan:(R,W)
```
Then `redwoodctl auth status` shows logged-in user. Ugly but works.

marie: We should also consider `redwoodctl auth login --out /full/path` so CI or installers can request the token be written to a specific path instead of relying on implicit user expansion. That would make automation reliable.

priya: Agreed. Proposal: add `--token-path` to `auth login` (and `--token-dir`). Also update the MSI to detect whether it's running elevated and if so either prompt for per-user target or write to ProgramData and set ACLs. Low-risk option: if elevated, the installer should not perform first-run auth automatically.

packaging: Noted. Current MSI repackager is using the `AllUsers` option but the postinstall script executed as SYSTEM wrote to the context user. We can change the postinstall to skip auth and add a guided note: "Run `redwoodctl auth login` as your user to finish onboarding." Alternatively document the `--token-path` for enterprise installs.

it-support-bot: NOTE: ticket created IT-4092 1 (installer: MSI writes token to elevated user profile; add token-path flag + ProgramData option).

ishaan: Another small UX quirk: after I copied token into my profile, `redwoodctl local-run` still failed because profiles were created in `C:\ProgramData\Redwood\profiles.yaml` by our infra image and CLI merged them but reported the system file as the active source. I had to set `REDWOOD_CONFIG_DIR` to my `%APPDATA%\Redwood` to force the dev override. Would be great if `redwoodctl profiles inspect <name>` told me which file supplied the active keys.

priya: Yep, adding `profiles inspect` and a `--config-dir` / `REDWOOD_CONFIG_DIR` env var are already on the short-term roadmap. We'll prioritize the MSI behavior and the token-path feature first.

marie: For enterprise, ProgramData approach is probably best: `C:\ProgramData\Redwood\profiles` for shared defaults and `%APPDATA%\Redwood` for per-user overrides, and the CLI should prefer per-user when both exist. We'll add an ACL checklist in the packaging notes.

ishaan: Happy to validate the MSI changes and test ProgramData flow. I'll attach the steps I used to IT ticket. Thanks!
thread_text: Installed Windows MSI on a shared dev VM; browser auth finished but regular user gets 'failed to read token: access denied' because token ended up in Administrator AppData.
